pageCache.pageTitle: Kingham Hill School | Independent School For Day and Boarding Pupils
pageCache.text:
Kingham Hill School
An independent, co-educational day and boarding school for pupils aged 11-18
Welcome to Kingham Hill
Dean Close Kingham Hill School is a vibrant, co-educational day and boarding school for pupils aged 11–18. Set in 105 acres of stunning Cotswold countryside, it offers the perfect environment in which to study, relax, and be active.
Despite its peaceful rural setting, the school is remarkably well connected: London Heathrow is just 90 minutes away, while direct rail services offer easy access to London (80 minutes) and Oxford (29 minutes), creating a rare balance of countryside tranquillity and convenient accessibility.
The best advertisement for a school is its pupils, and if you ask current parents why they chose Kingham Hill for their son or daughter, they invariably speak of the impression that friendly, happy, and well-balanced pupils made on them when visiting us.
We pride ourselves on our commitment to every individual pupil. Each young person is known, valued, and encouraged to develop their character, confidence, and talents to the fullest. Supported by experienced academic and pastoral staff, pupils thrive in an environment that combines intellectual curiosity and opportunity with exceptional pastoral care.
Get in Touch
We'd love to hear from you. Please contact our Admissions Team:
Mrs Debbie Marshall | 01608 731884 Mr Vlad Butin | 01608 731880
Email admissions@deanclosekingham.org.uk
Teaching and Learning
There is a science to learning and an art to teaching. At Kingham Hill, our teaching staff not only have excellent subject knowledge but commit to a professional learning culture, with excellent results.
Co-Curriculum
We are proud to offer a wide range of regular sports, clubs and activities that educate, enrich and engage our pupils. These activities are embedded into the school day as part of the daily timetable, or towards the end of each afternoon.
Day and Boarding
Every pupil belongs to one of ten houses that act as large, extended families. There are on average 15-40 pupils per house with a range of ages in each. We have four day and seven boarding houses which have their own inviting social lounges, games rooms and quiet rooms.
Sixth Form
The Sixth Form provides an environment in which pupils can flourish both academically and personally, balancing academic ambition with engagement in sport, activities, leadership, and service to others. We encourage pupils to take ownership of their individual journeys, while supporting and challenging them every step of the way, so that they grow into confident young adults who lead with integrity and purpose.
American Program
Kingham Hill School is one of only a handful of UK independent schools to offer a fully accredited US High School Diploma alongside the British curriculum. Set in the heart of the English countryside, our American Program combines academic flexibility with the enriching experience of British boarding, preparing students to thrive at leading universities in the US and around the world.

pageCache.pageTitle: Performing Arts Academy - Kingham Hill School
pageCache.text:
Performing Arts Academy
The creative arts have the power to inspire critical thinking, cultivate empathy, and encourage pupils to express themselves in ways that go beyond the traditional classroom. Our Performing Arts Academy takes place on a Monday after school, and provides pupils with the opportunity to explore a diverse range of activities, from classes and rehearsals to workshops, allowing them to pursue their individual passions. Activities include singing and choir, concert band, modern dance, script-writing workshops, theatre technology (lighting and sound), drama rehearsals, and, of course, preparations for our large-scale musical productions.
The Academy is based in Performing Arts Centre Theatre, the Music Department and our Drama Studios. Former Academy pupils have gone on to achieve remarkable success, with many joining the National Youth Theatre and gaining places at prestigious drama schools.
Our productions have covered a broad spectrum of genres over recent years, including Les Misérables, The Wizard of Oz, Grease, Jekyll and Hyde, The Crucible, The Addams Family and Billy Elliot. Senior pupils are also encouraged to take the reins, with many producing and directing their own plays under the guidance of our experienced staff.
In addition to the Academy, the Music Department offers a range of instrumental and choral ensembles. The Chapel Choir regularly performs at significant events such as Carol Services, Founders Day, Speech Day, and Remembrance Day. We also have a school orchestra that welcomes both advanced and intermediate players.
We take great pride in our Key Stage 3 Instrumental Scheme, where all 1st and 2nd Form pupils are given the chance to learn an orchestral instrument free of charge. Many of these pupils continue their musical journey in later years. Additionally, we provide individual lessons in a wide array of instruments, as well as voice.
For aspiring actors and dancers, the school offers LAMDA and dance lessons. Our LAMDA pupils consistently achieve outstanding results, and have the opportunity to share their talents at an annual LAMDA performance evening.

Current Opportunities
Dean Close Kingham Hill School is a supportive and rewarding place to work. Surrounded by glorious countryside and set in a stunning estate, it's a lovely place in which to spend your working day.
We warmly welcome applications from suitably qualified individuals. To explore current opportunities and submit your application, please visit the Dean Close Foundation Careers Site.
If the role in which you are interested is not available as a vacancy, please complete a Speculative Application and a member of the Recruitment Team will be in touch.

pageCache.pageTitle: Top Independent Schools Oxfordshire | Kingham Hill School
pageCache.text:
School History
Kingham Hill was purpose built by the Christian philanthropist Charles Edward Baring Young in 1886.
He put his faith into practice by establishing it as a place where boys with a boarding need could be educated and prepared for life.
Pupils learning stone masonry at the School in 1908
Kingham Hill staff and their families in 1894
In the early days the school was a virtually self-sufficient community. It had a farm, a wide range of workshops, a school building, a chapel, a sanatorium and various boarding houses. The Founder ensured that every Kingham child learned to read and write, gained a trade and had the benefit of understanding the Christian faith.
The Founder (centre) outside the present day Admin building in 1904. The chapel can be seen behind, with Severn and Greenwich yet to be built.
On leaving, the boys could progress to opportunities and new homes in London, or emigrate to a farm the Founder owned in Canada and make their life in the New World.
Outside Top School, 1934
Pupils at the School in 1947
Boys at the School in 1977
The Kingham Hill Trust, established by the Founder, administered the school until August 2025.
As of August 2025, Kingham Hill School became part of the Dean Close Foundation, a growing, vibrant and diverse family of independent schools and nurseries, uniting around a shared vision and set of values. These spring from the origins of Dean Close School, which was founded in 1886 in memory of Dean Francis Close, Rector of Cheltenham and educational philanthropist. The Christian ethos of that original school continues today, and the aim is that every child is given opportunities to flourish, underpinned by the core values of courage, contribution and love.
We continue the Founder's vision by providing an excellent all-round education, coupled with varied extra-curricular activities and experiences that thoroughly prepare our children to leave us as happy, rounded and resilient young people ready to succeed in their future lives.

Academic Results
At Kingham Hill, we are proud of the consistent academic success achieved by our pupils across GCSE, A Level, BTEC, and CTEC qualifications. Our results reflect a learning environment where high expectations, individual support, and a commitment to every pupil’s personal development combine to help young people achieve their best.
2025 Highlights
In the Sixth Form, over half of all results (53%) were awarded at A*–A (or equivalent), with 79% achieved at A*–B.
There was a 100% pass rate across vocational BTEC and CTEC courses, with more than half of all grades awarded at Distinction* or Distinction level.
At GCSE, 31% of results were awarded at grades 9–7, with 55% achieved at grades 9–6.
Over 80% of pupils secured places at their first-choice destinations, including the University of Bath, University of Bristol, Durham University, University of Edinburgh, University of Exeter, University of Leeds, Loughborough University, University of Manchester and the University of Oxford.
We are also delighted to celebrate two Oxbridge successes, with pupils securing places at the University of Oxford to study Biochemistry and the University of Cambridge to study Engineering.
"Our pupils have shown remarkable commitment and perseverance, and I couldn’t be prouder of their achievements. At Kingham Hill, our mission is to equip every pupil with the skills they need to thrive in life. The achievements we celebrate this year give our pupils the confidence to step boldly into their futures." Head, Mr Pete Last

Bursaries
Dean Close Kingham Hill School offers bursarial support in a variety of ways.
General Bursarial Support
The Dean Close Foundation offers a limited number of bursaries each year to pupils who would benefit from a Kingham Hill education but who are unable to afford the full fees. The number of children that we are able to help is limited to funds provided by the Foundation.
Bursaries are only available for pupils normally resident in the UK, for a maximum of 40% of fees and are means tested. In cases of particular need, the school can suggest a number of grant making trusts that may offer additional bursaries.
Bursary applications are made through our secure online portal. You will be required to create an account, through which you can submit and upload all the information required. For more information on bursary funding, please contact Mathew Madeley, Parent Finance Manager at mmadeley@deanclose.org.uk.
Please note that in order to apply for a Bursary, your child must be formally registered for a place at the school, or a current pupil.
Transformational Bursaries
140 years ago, philanthropist Charles Edward Baring Young founded Kingham Hill with a clear and generous vision: to provide opportunity and direction to young people of promise, regardless of background. Kingham Hill is proud of its founding purpose, which continues to shape its outlook and set it apart from many independent schools today.
We are proud to honour that legacy through a life-changing bursary programme, designed to open our doors to exceptional young people who might otherwise not have the chance to benefit from a Kingham Hill education. These Transformational Bursaries (a limited number of which are offered each year) go beyond financial support; they offer the opportunity to unlock potential, build confidence, and shape a future filled with possibility.
Who is this for?
We are looking for outstanding current Year 6, 7 and 8 pupils who demonstrate:
Bursaries are means-tested, ensuring support goes to families who need it most.
Academic promise or intellectual curiosity
Strong character, resilience, or leadership potential
What is offered?
Each award is flexible in value, reflecting the needs of the family and the potential of the child.
Significant financial support, tailored to individual circumstances
Access to a broad, enriching education
Why Kingham Hill?
For 140 years, Kingham Hill has been committed to transforming lives through education. Last year, the school became part of the Dean Close Foundation, placing it within a stable, forward-looking family of schools, and providing long-term security, shared expertise, and greater opportunities for pupils.
Set in 105 acres of stunning Cotswold countryside, Kingham Hill offers the perfect environment in which to study, relax, and be active. The school combines small class sizes with excellent facilities, including modern science laboratories and a state-of-the-art Sports Centre. Its unique campus also features a working school farm, alongside opportunities such as the Combined Cadet Force, helping pupils build resilience, teamwork, and practical skills.
Just as importantly, Kingham Hill is consistently praised for its outstanding pastoral care and community-focused environment where pupils feel known, valued, and encouraged to achieve their full potential.
Take the First Step
If you believe your child — or a pupil you know — could benefit from this opportunity, we encourage you to contact our admissions team on 01608 731844.
Alternatively email Admissions@Deanclosekingham.org.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: Equipped to Flourish - Kingham Hill School
pageCache.text:
Equipped to Flourish
Equipped to Flourish (ETF) is the foundation upon which everything we do at Kingham Hill is built, underpinned by the School’s informal motto, ‘work hard, play hard, serve well’. Its themes are woven into every aspect of school life with the aim of supporting our pupils as they grow and develop in character, enabling them to flourish both at school and beyond.
The Four Key Themes
The ability to keep going. Treating success and failure the same.
Taking ownership, being accountable and not blaming or relying on others.
The ability to work with others. Not thinking less of yourself but of yourself less.
Staying true to yourself when no-one's looking and even under pressure.

Health Centre
Our Health Centre enjoys well equipped, purpose-built facilities and is open during the school day. Emergency cover is readily available around the clock and we enjoy a formal relationship with Chipping Norton Health Centre.
We have a great team of two experienced nursing sisters; Elaine Barton and Mary Garner.
Elaine originally trained in Northampton and qualified in 1988. She has experience in accident and emergency care, practice nursing and in the private sector in endoscopy nursing and most recently carrying out immunisations in local schools. She also has experience in fostering children with both emotional and physical problems. She has attended numerous courses, including those in diabetes, spirometry and asthma.
Mary is an experienced school nursing sister, having previously worked at Marlborough College and Bloxham School. Her nursing career has also included senior staff nurse positions in operating theatres in Oxfordshire hospitals. Mary has a wealth of experience in dealing with all the issues that can arise at an independent boarding school. Following an initial stint as the Relief Nursing Sister in June 2013, she joined the team permanently in January 2015.
We are delighted that the running of the Health Centre is in such experienced and capable hands. Elaine and Mary are always ready to handle pupil enquiries and concerns.

Alumni Ambassadors Programme
At Kingham Hill School, we are proud of our vibrant and diverse alumni community. To help foster stronger connections amongst Hillians — and between alumni and the school — we’ve launched the Alumni Ambassadors Programme, a key part of our wider engagement strategy.
What is the Alumni Ambassadors Programme?
The programme invites Hillians to take on the role of Alumni Ambassadors, helping to connect fellow alumni, organise gatherings, and build meaningful networks around shared experiences and interests.
How it works:
Each Ambassador will work with the school to help set up and lead an alumni group, which could be based on:
School year – defined by the year you would have left if you had stayed through to the Sixth Form.
Year cohorts – groups spanning five-year intervals (e.g., 1990–1995 leavers).
Shared interests – such as sports, arts, music, academic subjects, or professional fields.
These groups offer opportunities for alumni to reconnect, network, mentor, and support each other and the school — whether through informal meet-ups, online communities, or special events. The school will provide Ambassadors with guidance and support, including communications, promotion, and help co-ordinating events.
Interested in becoming an Ambassador?
If you’re passionate about Kingham Hill and would like to bring people together, we’d love to hear from you. Our Ambassadors play an important role in sustaining the spirit and values of the Hillian community — wherever life has taken them.
To find out more or express your interest, please contact Alumni Engagement and Development Lead, Andrew Mitchell on 01608 731887 or via alumni@kinghamhill.org.

Newsletters
The newsletter is shared with a wide audience, including recent leavers, long-standing alumni, and friends, offering updates from across the school, news of fellow alumni, and a glimpse into current school life. We hope it serves as a meaningful link to the school and to one another.
We invite you to explore the archive below and revisit any editions you may have missed. As always, we warmly welcome your news, memories, and reflections.

American Program
Discover a world-class education in the heart of the English countryside. Kingham Hill School’s American Program combines an American curriculum with the advantages of a British boarding school experience.
This unique program prepares students for a seamless transition to top universities in the US and beyond. Designed for students seeking a US-style education abroad, the American Program curriculum is designed to mirror the expectations of US high schools, whilst offering additional opportunities for personal growth and development within the context of a British school environment.
“As a family planning to return to the US, Kingham Hill’s American Program was exactly what we needed. Our child is connected to the US curriculum whilst still having the great experience of being at a British School.”
American Program Parent
US High School Diploma: Upon successful completion, students are awarded a US-style high school diploma, ensuring that their education is recognised by universities and colleges across the US and internationally.
Advanced Placement (AP) Courses: Students can choose from a selection of AP courses that provide the opportunity to earn college credit while still in high school.
Personalised Academic Support: Each student has a dedicated tutor and also receives guidance from our Senior Academic team on course selection, university applications, and personal development.
College Preparatory Focus: The American Program is structured to meet the academic and extracurricular needs of students who are preparing for university in the United States.
Fully Accredited: The American Program at Kingham Hill is accredited by the Middle States Association of Schools and Colleges (MSA-CESS).
Our American Program offers a wide range of courses that cater to students’ interests and prepare them for university success. In addition to the core subjects, students can choose from specialised subjects that reflect both their academic strengths and future aspirations.
Advanced Placement (AP) Courses: We currently offer a selection of AP courses either in school or through our online course provider, which offer university level material and the opportunity to earn college credits. These rigorous courses prepare students for competitive university admissions and provide a strong academic foundation for future study.
Electives & Specialised Subjects: In addition, students can choose from a variety of electives that allow for exploration in diverse areas.
Education at Kingham Hill extends far beyond academics. Students are encouraged to discover their interests, develop leadership skills, and grow as individuals. Opportunities available in:
Boarding: Boarding life fosters independence, resilience, and lifelong friendships, whilst maintaining a strong sense of belonging and care
Students in the American Program learn alongside peers from the UK and around the world, gaining valuable cultural understanding and international perspective - essential preparation for university and life beyond school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Teaching and Learning at Kingham Hill School
pageCache.text:
Academic Overview
Our goal is to inspire a passion for learning in our pupils whilst equipping them with the skills necessary for independent and critical thinking - skills that allow them to follow an argument to its conclusion, appreciate excellence in all its forms, and develop sound judgment and discernment.
In their early years at Kingham Hill, Lower School (1st - 3rd Form) pupils study a broad range of subjects. Alongside the core subjects of English, Maths and Science, their timetable also includes Art, Design & Technology, Digital Literacy, Drama, French, Geography, History, Music, Physical Education, Spanish and Theology. Pupils are encouraged to embrace new challenges and make the most of the co-curricular activities on offer to them as they develop their interests and independent learning skills. This broad foundation sets the stage for future choices in GCSEs, A Levels, vocational qualifications, or our American Diploma route.
Central to our academic success is a highly qualified and dedicated staff. At Kingham Hill, teachers are experts in their fields, and they are passionate about the subjects that they teach. Each pupil is supported by a personal tutor who monitors progress and provides daily guidance. Our academic society, Octagon, offers enrichment opportunities beyond the standard curriculum for our most capable pupils.
Our Greens Department, specialising in learning support, has the expertise to deliver tailored interventions where needed. All staff in Greens work closely with the wider teaching team and Heads of Departments to ensure correct support is given throughout the school. Enabling pupils to become independent, excited learners whilst providing them with effective strategies to succeed is at the heart of the Department.
Above all, we aim to nurture innate curiosity and a drive for achievement in every pupil, no matter what their strengths. Education, for us, is not merely a means to an end; our academic philosophy is centered on fostering a lifelong love of learning, which naturally leads to greater success in all areas of life.

Boarding
A Friendly, Family Atmosphere
Kingham Hill has five boarding houses, each with its own distinct character and atmosphere, where pupils are treated as a part of a large, extended family. Every House is supported by a dedicated team of experienced Houseparents, Pastoral Assistants, and Matrons, who provide care and guidance around the clock.
The Houses are designed for comfort and community, featuring spacious bedrooms, study areas, common rooms, and recreational facilities where pupils can relax and unwind after a busy school day. Accommodation ranges from dormitories housing four to eight pupils, to single rooms for older pupils.
Our vibrant boarding community brings together pupils from across the UK, including HM Forces families, alongside children from the US and other international backgrounds, creating a rich and diverse environment for learning, friendship, and personal growth.
Flexi, Weekly and Full Boarding
Boarding at Kingham Hill is an experience that fosters a sense of independence, resilience, and community with flexible boarding options to suit the needs of each and every child, including full, weekly and flexi boarding.
Full-time boarders enjoy a home-away-from-home experience, living in a safe and supportive environment where they can focus on their studies and enjoy the raft of extracurricular activities available to them throughout the week and at weekends. Weekly boarders enjoy the same, returning home at the weekends, while flexi-boarders have the flexibility to choose when they stay in the boarding house.
An Enriching Experience
Boarding at Kingham Hill offers pupils a wealth of opportunities to develop their interests and talents outside the classroom with a wide range of extracurricular activities, including sports, music, drama, and outdoor pursuits. Pupils can also take part in a variety of clubs and societies, such as debating, chess, and swimming.
The sense of community at Kingham Hill is what makes the school, and boarding in particular, so special, with pupils from different backgrounds and cultures coming together to form friendships which continue long after they leave.
